This works even when keen-pbr itself is broken, because the removal scripts never run it. If dnsmasq would be left without any upstream DNS server (it has no-resolv and no server= line of its own), the servers from dnsmasq-fallback.conf stay in a block marked keen-pbr fallback upstream in /opt/etc/dnsmasq.conf (Keenetic) or /etc/dnsmasq.conf (Debian). Replace them with your own. Firewall rules left behind by a keen-pbr that crashed are removed as well.

Troubleshooting

See Per-list DNS servers do not work.

item.title: keen-pbr CLI usage
item.description:
keen-pbr can run the service, inspect live routing state, download list data, and test routing decisions.

The status, download and test-routing commands talk to the running service. If the service is not running, they fail with exit code 1. Start the service first (on a router it starts with the system).

Usage 

Usage: keen-pbr [options] <command>

Options:
  --config <path>    Path to JSON config file (default: <KEEN_PBR_DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH>)
  --log-level <lvl>  Log level: error, warn, info, verbose, debug (default: info)
  --log-target <target>  Log destination: stderr, syslog, or both (default: both)
  --pid-file <path>  Override daemon.pid_file when running the service command
  --crash-report <path>  Last-crash report path (default: /tmp/keen-pbr-crash.log)
  --no-api           Disable REST API at runtime
  --use-raw-prerouting  Use raw PREROUTING for IPv4 forwarded traffic (iptables only)
  --use-raw6-prerouting Use raw PREROUTING for IPv6 forwarded traffic (iptables only)
  --version          Show version and exit
  --help             Show this help and exit

Commands:
  service                            Start the routing service (foreground)
  status                             Show routing/firewall status and exit
  download                           Download all configured lists to cache and exit
  test-routing <ip-or-domain> [packet options]
                                     Test expected vs actual routing for an IP or domain
      --proto <tcp|udp|other>        Packet protocol
      --src-addr <ip>                Packet source address
      --src-port <port>              Packet source port
      --dest-port <port>             Packet destination port
      --dscp <0-63>                  Packet DSCP (default: 0)
  generate-resolver-config dnsmasq   Print the dnsmasq config generated from dns.rules/dns.fallback (cached lists only; used as dnsmasq conf-script, always exits 0)
  dnsmasq detect [--json]            List dnsmasq instances, their DNS endpoints and which one keen-pbr uses
  dnsmasq remove <selector>          Restart one dnsmasq instance without keen-pbr's generated config (OpenWrt: also return the moved servers)
  dnsmasq finish-upgrade <keep|off>  After an upgrade from 3.3.x: keep dnsmasq management on or turn it off, and stamp the config version
  hash-password [--update]           Generate an authentication password hash; --update writes config.json

The config file is usually /etc/keen-pbr/config.json on OpenWrt and Debian, and /opt/etc/keen-pbr/config.json on Keenetic / NetCraze.

Options

Flag Description
--config <path> Path to the JSON config file. Works only with the service command.
--log-level <lvl> Log verbosity: error, warn, info, verbose, or debug.
--log-target <target> External log destination: stderr, syslog, or both. Defaults to both for every command. The packaged service files (systemd, OpenWrt procd, Keenetic init script) pass --log-target syslog so logs are not duplicated when stdout/stderr are also captured by the init system.
--pid-file <path> Path to the PID file (the file holding the service’s process number). Replaces daemon.pid_file from the config; service only.
--crash-report <path> Where to write the report about the last crash. Defaults to /tmp/keen-pbr-crash.log.
--no-api Disable the REST API even if enabled in config.
--use-raw-prerouting Opt in to raw-table IPv4 forwarded-traffic classification; available only with iptables.
--use-raw6-prerouting Opt in to raw-table IPv6 forwarded-traffic classification; available only with iptables.
--version Print version and exit.
--help Print help and exit.

--use-raw-prerouting

This flag is mainly for Keenetic / NetCraze. The firmware periodically rebuilds the mangle firewall table, and keen-pbr’s rules briefly disappear. With this flag keen-pbr puts the rules for IPv4 traffic passing through the router into the raw table, which the firmware does not rebuild. IPv6 has a separate flag, --use-raw6-prerouting.

On Keenetic / NetCraze the start script sets these flags. The mode is set with KEEN_PBR_RAW_PREROUTING in /opt/etc/keen-pbr/defaults:

Value What it does
auto (default) Checks separately for IPv4 and IPv6 whether raw works, and uses it if so; otherwise mangle
disable Always use mangle
enable Require raw for IPv4 and IPv6. If raw is unavailable, the service does not start
ipv4-only, ipv6-only Require raw for one address family only

Restart the service after changing it. The practical difference between the modes is described in Keenetic / NetCraze installation.

To check whether raw is available:

ls -l "/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/iptable_raw.ko"
ls -l "/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/ip6table_raw.ko"
grep -x raw /proc/net/ip_tables_names
grep -x raw /proc/net/ip6_tables_names
iptables -t raw -S
ip6tables -t raw -S

Commands

Command Description
service Start the routing service in the foreground.
status Show service, outbound, routing, firewall and kernel health, then the issue list the web UI overview shows, and exit. Exits with 1 when any check failed or any issue is an error.
download [--reload] Download all URL-backed lists into the cache and exit. With --reload the service applies the lists that changed right away.
generate-resolver-config dnsmasq Print the dnsmasq configuration for per-list DNS servers.
hash-password [--update] Create a password hash for logging in to the web UI and API.
dnsmasq detect [--json] List dnsmasq instances, their DNS endpoints and the instance keen-pbr uses.
dnsmasq remove <selector> Restart one dnsmasq instance without keen-pbr’s config.
dnsmasq finish-upgrade <keep|off> After an upgrade from 3.3.x, keep dnsmasq management on (keep) or turn it off (off). Writes the version field to the config. Restart the service afterwards.
test-routing <ip-or-domain> [packet options] Compare expected and actual routing for the given IP or domain. The daemon runs the check, the same way as the routing test in the web UI.

generate-resolver-config dnsmasq

When dns.resolver_integration: "dnsmasq" is enabled, this command prints the dnsmasq configuration built by keen-pbr. Lists are taken from the cache only; nothing is downloaded. It contains domain-to-server mappings, DNS rebinding protection exceptions, and fallback servers.

Usage:

keen-pbr generate-resolver-config dnsmasq

Output: Dnsmasq configuration directives.

# Generated by keen-pbr - do not edit manually

address=/use-application-dns.net/

server=192.168.1.1

# List: ai_services
server=/openai.com/www.openai.com/.../1.1.1.1
rebind-domain-ok=/openai.com/www.openai.com/...

Behavior:

  • Always exits with status 0, even on errors; errors are printed as # keen-pbr: ... comment lines.
  • When resolver_integration: "none" (default), or the config cannot be read, the output is only the server= lines from dnsmasq-fallback.conf; the dynamic sets are filled by interception.
  • With "dnsmasq" and no fallback servers, those server= lines are added to the output.
  • dnsmasq reads the config via this command (see conf-script=keen-pbr generate-resolver-config dnsmasq in the drop-in ).

hash-password

Creates a password hash for logging in to the web UI and API. The command asks for the password twice.

keen-pbr hash-password
keen-pbr hash-password --update

Without --update the command prints Password hash: <hash>, which you paste into api.authentication.password_hash yourself. With --update it writes api.enabled: true, api.authentication.enabled: true and the hash into config.json. Then restart the service: Restart the keen-pbr service for authentication changes to take effect.

dnsmasq detect and remove

Inspect and clean up the dnsmasq integration without the daemon. Neither command needs the control socket.

keen-pbr dnsmasq detect [--json]
keen-pbr dnsmasq remove <selector>

detect lists every dnsmasq instance the platform hook reports: whether it runs, its DNS endpoint and how it was confirmed, listening sockets, whether keen-pbr’s drop-in is installed and which configuration it loaded, and any problem. The last line tells which instance keen-pbr selected and how (explicit, adopted or automatic), or why it could not choose.

dnsmasq hook: /usr/lib/keen-pbr/dnsmasq-hook.sh (platform openwrt, binary /usr/sbin/dnsmasq)

  uci:cfg01411c  [selected: adopted]
    running:     yes (pid 1842)
    enabled:     yes
    endpoint:    127.0.0.1:53 (stamp_verified)
    listeners:   udp+tcp 0.0.0.0:53, udp+tcp [::]:53
    keen-pbr:    installed, loaded hash 3f2a9c0e1b7d4a55c6e8f0a1b2c3d4e5
    conf-dir:    /tmp/dnsmasq.cfg01411c.d (included)
    problem:     none

Selection: uci:cfg01411c (adopted)
  • --json prints the same data as one JSON object (selected, selection, error_code, message, warnings, instances[]).
  • Exit code 0 when an instance is selected and has no problem, 1 otherwise.
  • If the choice is ambiguous, the output ends with a hint to set dns.dnsmasq_instance.

remove <selector> restarts one instance so that it stops using keen-pbr’s config; on OpenWrt it also returns the server list moved aside. Use it when detect shows an instance that still runs keen-pbr’s config after you switched the integration off.

  • Must run as root. Exit code 64 for a missing or invalid selector.
  • If the integration is still enabled for this instance, the command prints a note: the daemon may apply its config to dnsmasq again on its next sync. Disable the integration first.

Signals

You can control the running keen-pbr service with signals:

Signal Action
SIGUSR1 Rebuild routes and firewall rules
SIGHUP Re-read config.json and apply it again. Does not work in the keen-pbr-headless build
SIGTERM / SIGINT Graceful shutdown

Example: re-read the config with SIGHUP:

bash
kill -HUP $(cat /var/run/keen-pbr.pid)

Examples

Check live routing and firewall state:

bash
keen-pbr status

Example output:

keen-pbr status - config: /etc/keen-pbr/config.json
Service: running (runtime running: startup complete) - keen-pbr 3.4.0 (build 20261012064940)
Firewall backend: nftables

Outbounds:
  corp_vpn [interface] iface=corp_vpn fwmark=0x00010000 table=402
    state ........................................................... HEALTHY
    route   table=402 default dev corp_vpn ............................... OK
    rule    0x00010000/0x00ff0000 -> table=402 pri=402 ........... OK [v4+v6]
  auto_vpn [urltest] fwmark=0x00060000 table=402
    state ........................................................... HEALTHY
    member  corp_vpn (corp_vpn) 41 ms ................................ ACTIVE
    member  backup_vpn (wg1) ....................................... DEGRADED
      probe failed: timeout
    route   table=402 default dev corp_vpn ............................... OK
    rule    0x00060000/0x00ff0000 -> table=402 pri=407 ........... OK [v4+v6]

Firewall:
  chain   KeenPbrTable / prerouting hook ............................... OK
  rule    kpbr4_generic -> MARK 0x00010000 ........................ MISSING
    rule not found in nftables prerouting chain
  rule    kpbr4_auto -> MARK 0x00060000 selected=corp_vpn .............. OK

Kernel 6.12.94:
  capability nfqueue ................................................... OK
  probe      set_write ................................................. OK
  probe      conntrack ................................................. OK

Interception: running, DNS hold active, L7 active
dnsmasq: ok, alive, 127.0.0.1:53 (uci:cfg01411c), 3 rules, 16 domains

Issues:
  ERROR  Firewall rules do not match: 1
         kpbr4_generic: rule not found in nftables prerouting chain
  WARN   auto_vpn: failing members: 1
         backup_vpn · degraded · probe failed: timeout

Overall: DEGRADED (1 check(s) failed, 1 error(s), 1 warning(s))
Status values: OK / MISSING / MISMATCH / ERROR

Download all URL-backed lists:

bash
keen-pbr download

The command prints the service’s answer as one JSON line. refreshed_lists holds the lists that were updated, changed_lists those whose content changed:

{"ok":true,"protocol_version":2,"request_id":"cli-download","result":{"changed_lists":["google"],"failed_lists":[],"refreshed_lists":["google"],"reloaded":false}}

If a list fails to download, the command prints an error and exits with code 1.

Compare expected and actual routing:

bash
keen-pbr test-routing google.com

Example output:

Target: google.com
Resolved IPs: 2001:4860:4860::8888, 142.250.74.14

IP                        | List Match               | Expected Outbound  | Actual Outbound    | Status
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2001:4860:4860::8888      | google (via google.com)  | corp_vpn           | corp_vpn           | OK
142.250.74.14             | google (via google.com)  | corp_vpn           | corp_vpn           | OK

By default only list membership is checked. To also match rules that use ports, protocol, source address or DSCP, describe the packet:

Flag Description
--proto <tcp|udp|other> Packet protocol.
--src-addr <ip> Source address of the client sending the packet.
--src-port <port> Source port.
--dest-port <port> Destination port.
--dscp <0-63> DSCP value. A packet without --dscp is treated as DSCP 0.
bash
keen-pbr test-routing google.com --proto tcp --dest-port 443 --src-addr 192.168.1.10

If a rule depends on a field you did not give (for example src_addr), that IP shows (unknown).

item.title: Advanced
item.description:
Most users can skip this page.

These settings are for advanced setups and service-level tuning: daemon, api, fwmark, iproute, and lists_autoupdate.

Some of these settings are in the web UI: General > Settings > General, Lists autoupdate and Advanced routing settings. The low-level fields appear after you switch Settings mode to Advanced. This page describes every config.json field; next to a field you will find where it is in the UI.

daemon

Controls the PID file path (the file holding the service’s process number), the cache directory, and general routing behaviour.

Field Type Default Description
pid_file string — Path to write the PID file. Can be overridden with the --pid-file flag
cache_dir string /var/cache/keen-pbr Directory for cached list data
firewall_backend string "auto" Which firewall to use: auto (pick automatically), iptables, or nftables
clear_dynamic_sets_on_apply boolean false Clear the dynamic sets (domain IP addresses collected from DNS replies and connections) on every config apply or service restart. List refreshes and link switches never clear them. Web UI: Clear learned domain addresses on apply.
ipset_hashsize integer absent Optional initial hash table size for ipsets created by the iptables backend (default 1024). Has no effect with nftables. Must be between 1 and 2147483648. Web UI (Advanced mode): IPSet hash table size (ipset hashsize). Changing it recreates the sets and empties the dynamic sets.
ipset_maxelem integer absent Optional maximum element count for ipsets created by the iptables backend (default 65536). Has no effect with nftables. Must be between 1 and 4294967295. Web UI: Maximum entries in ipset (ipset maxelem). Changing it recreates the sets and empties the dynamic sets.
reuse_static_sets_on_runtime_refresh boolean true Do not refill list sets on SIGUSR1, urltest/icmptest switches and interface state changes: only rules are updated, which is faster. If false, sets are refilled every time.
skip_marked_packets boolean true Do not process packets that another program has already marked. Web UI: Skip packets that are already marked.
ipv6_enabled boolean true Route IPv6 traffic. When false, IPv6 flows as usual, bypassing keen-pbr. Web UI: Enable IPv6 support.
strict_enforcement boolean false If the interface or gateway of an interface outbound is down, do not let its traffic go out through the normal connection: the outbound’s table gets the route from strict_enforcement_action instead. Can be set per outbound. Web UI: Block traffic when an outbound is unavailable (kill-switch).
strict_enforcement_action string "unreachable" What to do with traffic under strict_enforcement: unreachable returns an immediate network error; blackhole silently drops packets until the application times out.
max_file_size_bytes integer 8388608 (8 MiB) Maximum allowed size in bytes for downloaded remote list content
firewall_verify_max_bytes integer 262144 How many bytes of iptables/nft output to read when checking firewall rules (keen-pbr status, status page); 0 means no limit
exec_timeout_seconds integer 30 How many seconds to wait for keen-pbr’s helper scripts (for example the dnsmasq script) before stopping them. Minimum 1.
exec_kill_grace_seconds integer 2 How many seconds to give a script to exit after it is stopped before it is killed. Minimum 0.
config.json
{
  "daemon": {
    "pid_file": "/var/run/keen-pbr.pid",
    "cache_dir": "/var/cache/keen-pbr",
    "firewall_backend": "auto",
    "clear_dynamic_sets_on_apply": false,
    "ipset_hashsize": null,
    "ipset_maxelem": null,
    "reuse_static_sets_on_runtime_refresh": true,
    "skip_marked_packets": true,
    "ipv6_enabled": true,
    "strict_enforcement": false,
    "strict_enforcement_action": "unreachable",
    "max_file_size_bytes": 8388608,
    "firewall_verify_max_bytes": 262144,
    "exec_timeout_seconds": 30,
    "exec_kill_grace_seconds": 2
  }
}

The cache directory stores downloaded remote lists so they are available if the network is unreachable at startup.

api

Controls the embedded HTTP API server that the web UI runs on.

Field Type Default Description
enabled boolean false Enable the HTTP API and the web UI. The config installed by the keen-pbr package already has it on
listen string "0.0.0.0:12121" Address and port to listen on
max_request_body_bytes integer 1048576 Maximum request body size in bytes. Minimum 1024.
read_timeout_seconds integer 15 How many seconds to wait for a request from the client. Minimum 1.
write_timeout_seconds integer 15 How many seconds to send a response to the client. Minimum 1.
keep_alive_timeout_seconds integer 20 How many seconds to keep a connection open between requests. Minimum 1.
authentication object off Password login: enabled and password_hash. With enabled: true the hash is required. Create it with keen-pbr hash-password --update or in the web UI: Security.
cors.allowed_origins array — Site addresses (origins) allowed to call the API from a browser, for example "https://router.example". Exact http:// or https:// addresses only, no path or wildcards.
config.json
{
  "api": {
    "enabled": true,
    "listen": "0.0.0.0:12121",
    "max_request_body_bytes": 1048576,
    "read_timeout_seconds": 15,
    "write_timeout_seconds": 15,
    "keep_alive_timeout_seconds": 20,
    "authentication": { "enabled": false },
    "cors": { "allowed_origins": [] }
  }
}

Start keen-pbr with --no-api to disable the API regardless of the config. See REST API for endpoint documentation and runtime controls.

fwmark

Sets the range of fwmark values. A fwmark is a label keen-pbr puts on a packet so the system sends it to the right routing table (the table holding one outbound’s routes). See fwmark and conntrack.

Field Type Default Description
start string "0x00010000" First fwmark value to assign to outbounds. Web UI: fwmark starting value
mask string "0x00FF0000" Fwmark bitmask. Web UI: fwmark mask
config.json
{
  "fwmark": {
    "start": "0x00010000",
    "mask": "0x00FF0000"
  }
}

mask must be a run of hex F digits, for example 0x00FF0000. Outbounds get sequential fwmark values starting from start, within mask.

If other software on your system uses the same fwmark range, adjust start and mask to avoid conflicts.

iproute

Sets the routing table numbers and the priorities of the ip rule entries that keen-pbr creates for outbounds. An ip rule entry is a rule that picks a routing table by fwmark.

Field Type Default Description
table_start integer 150 First routing table ID to allocate for outbounds. Web UI: IP routing table starting value
rule_priority_start integer or null table_start Priority of the first ip rule entry; null means the same as table_start
process_router_traffic boolean false Apply route rules to traffic of the router itself and collect domain IPs from it. When false, keen-pbr handles only traffic of devices in the network. detour of DNS servers works either way. Web UI (Advanced mode): Process router’s own traffic.
config.json
{
  "iproute": {
    "table_start": 150,
    "rule_priority_start": null,
    "process_router_traffic": false
  }
}

Outbounds are assigned sequential table IDs starting from table_start. Check that these IDs do not clash with existing routing tables. Do not start from reserved IDs: 0, 128, 250-260 and everything from 32000. A config with such a table_start fails validation, and reserved IDs are skipped when numbers are allocated.

When keen-pbr stops, it removes only its own routes. Routes added by you or by other software stay in place.

Failover

Rules are checked top to bottom and the first match wins. Two identical rules with different outbounds therefore do not give you a backup: packets never reach the second rule.

If the first outbound’s interface goes down, the result depends on strict_enforcement:

  • off (the default): traffic falls back to the ISP’s default gateway, bypassing the VPN;
  • on: traffic is blocked (strict_enforcement_action decides how).

To switch traffic to a backup link, create one urltest outbound and put both interfaces in it. conntrack_on_switch controls what happens to open connections when urltest moves to a faster link: preserve (the default) keeps them on the old link, delete deletes their conntrack entries, so applications reconnect through the new one. When the selected link stops working, conntrack entries of its connections are always deleted.

Good to know

  • With ipv6_enabled: false, IPv6 traffic flows as usual, bypassing keen-pbr.
  • keen-pbr learns domain IPs from ordinary DNS replies passing through the router, even when a client uses a third-party DNS server. If a device uses encrypted DNS ( DoH , DoT ), keen-pbr learns the site’s address only from the connection itself (the server name in TLS, HTTP or QUIC ), and the first connections may bypass the VPN. To avoid this, turn off “secure DNS” on the device and set up DoH/DoT on the router itself.
  • When a learned domain IP expires from a list, new connections take a different route, while connections that are already open keep their route, because their fwmark is stored in conntrack .
  • keen-pbr download downloads lists into the cache. To make the running service use them, run keen-pbr download --reload or restart the service.
  • If keen-pbr stopped after a crash, do not change fwmark.mask before the next start: otherwise it will not recognise its old rules and cannot remove them. If that has already happened, reboot the router.

One instance only

Run only one keen-pbr per router. A separate pid_file does not help: a second instance uses the same firewall rule and set names and breaks the first one’s rules.

Put all outbounds and routing rules into one configuration. If you need two independent instances, run them in separate network namespaces.

lists_autoupdate

Scheduled refresh of remote lists.

If the lists_autoupdate section is omitted, automatic refresh is disabled. In the web UI: General > Settings > Lists autoupdate.

Field Type Default Description
enabled boolean false Enable automatic list refresh. Web UI: Enable lists autoupdate
cron string — Refresh schedule: a 5-field cron expression (format below). Web UI: Refresh schedule
config.json
{
  "lists_autoupdate": {
    "enabled": true,
    "cron": "0 4 * * 0"
  }
}

The cron format: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. The example above runs weekly at 04:00 on Sunday.

If cron is filled in, it is validated even when enabled is false. With enabled: true it is required.

If a remote list could not be downloaded at startup, the daemon keeps retrying it in the background with increasing delays (10 seconds, 30 seconds, 2 minutes, then every 5 minutes) until it succeeds. This does not depend on lists_autoupdate.

You can refresh the lists by hand at any time:

keen-pbr download --reload

item.title: REST API
item.description:
The REST API lets scripts and external systems control and monitor keen-pbr. For example:

  • Prometheus and Grafana show VPN channel health and latency (see GET /metrics).
  • A cron job refreshes lists on a schedule through POST /api/lists/refresh.
  • A script restarts routing through POST /api/service/restart.

If you only use the web interface, you can skip this page.

The REST API is available when:

  • Full package version is installed (keen-pbr, not keen-pbr-headless)
  • The config has api.enabled: true
  • The --no-api flag was not passed at startup

Configuration

In the web interface, open Security > Authentication and CORS. Turn on Enable authentication, enter a New password and confirm it. If a website on another address must call the API from a browser, add its address to Allowed CORS origins (one per line). Changes take effect immediately.

Set the device name in General > Settings > General > Device name. It appears in the browser tab title and under the keen-pbr logo, which helps tell several routers apart.

The same settings in config.json:

config.json
{
  "device_name": "Home router",
  "api": {
    "enabled": true,
    "listen": "0.0.0.0:12121",
    "authentication": {
      "enabled": true,
      "password_hash": "argon2id$v=19$m=2048,t=2,p=1$..."
    },
    "cors": {
      "allowed_origins": ["https://panel.example.com"]
    }
  }
}

device_name is optional and may be empty.

If you edit config.json by hand, generate the password hash with this command (it asks for the password):

keen-pbr hash-password

To write the hash straight into the file, run keen-pbr --config /path/to/config.json hash-password --update. Then restart the keen-pbr service: the daemon does not notice changes made to the file from outside.

The password is stored as an Argon2id hash. Hashes from older keen-pbr versions do not work: set the password again.

When authentication is on, requests to the API use one of two methods:

  • Basic authentication: username admin and your password (curl -u admin:password ...).
  • Bearer token: a temporary key issued by POST /api/auth/login and sent in the header Authorization: Bearer <token>. A token is valid for 24 hours. Only one token is valid at a time: a new login, including one in the web interface, cancels the previous one. After the daemon restarts, get a new token.

Without logging in, only GET /api/auth/status and POST /api/auth/login are available. /metrics is protected like the rest of the API.

When authentication is off, requests from other websites in a browser are blocked. When it is on, addresses from Allowed CORS origins are allowed, as well as Chrome and Firefox extensions. The password travels over the network in clear text, so use a trusted network or HTTPS through a reverse proxy (a web server in front of keen-pbr).

By default, the API listens on 0.0.0.0:12121 (api.listen). All routes are served at that address.

The OpenAPI document is the complete request and response schema. The main routes are listed below (an outbound is a channel that traffic goes through: a VPN interface, your ISP, or a block):

Route Purpose
GET /api/health/service Service, config draft, current start/stop operation, and rollback status.
POST /api/service/start, /stop, /restart Start, stop, or restart routing asynchronously.
GET /api/config, POST /api/config Read or stage a validated config draft.
GET /api/config/defaults Default values for settings that are not set in the config.
POST /api/config/discard, /save, /rollback Discard a draft, save and apply it, or return to the previous config after a failed apply.
GET /api/status/events Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream: the server pushes changes, so you do not need to poll. Events: snapshot (full state on connect), service, outbounds, interfaces, issues, routing, auth, config. A keep-alive signal arrives every 15 seconds. The config event carries only a revision number; read the data with GET /api/config. After a dropped connection, the new connection starts with a fresh snapshot.
GET /api/health/issues Detected problems and kernel check results: the same list as the overview page and keen-pbr status.
GET /api/runtime/outbounds, /api/runtime/interfaces Current outbound state and the list of system interfaces.
GET /api/health/routing, POST /api/routing/test Routing and firewall diagnostics, and a route check for a specific domain or IP address.
POST /api/lists/refresh Refresh one or all remote URL lists.
GET /api/dns/test Stream of DNS and TLS/QUIC interception events, or the DNS check in the web interface.
GET /api/diagnostics/command-failure Log of recent system command failures.
GET /metrics Prometheus text metrics.
/api/auth/status, /api/auth/login, /api/auth/logout, /api/auth/password, /api/auth/settings Authentication status, login and logout, password (GET shows whether one is set; POST sets a new one), and authentication and CORS settings.

GET /api/health/service

Returns the running daemon version and routing runtime status.

bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:12121/api/health/service

Response 

{
  "version": "3.4.0",
  "build": "20261010120000",
  "status": "running",
  "runtime_state": "running",
  "runtime_state_reason": "config apply complete",
  "os_type": "debian",
  "os_version": "12",
  "build_variant": "generic",
  "config_is_draft": false,
  "rollback_available": false
}

status is running, degraded (DNS interception is enabled but unavailable) or stopped.

When interception is enabled, the response includes an intercept object: whether DNS interception (dns_hold_active) and traffic analysis (l7_active) are active, the kernel features available (nfqueue, nflog, connbytes, addrtype), and counters of processed packets, errors and queue overruns ( NFQUEUE /NFLOG). These values are mostly useful for diagnostics.

For channel state (health, latency) see GET /api/runtime/outbounds.

GET /metrics

Returns metrics in Prometheus text format 0.0.4. Prometheus requests this address periodically (a scrape) and stores the values. Authentication is the same as for the API: use Basic authentication or the current Bearer token. If metrics are unavailable, the response is 503:

curl -u admin:password http://127.0.0.1:12121/metrics

All durations are in seconds (fractional numbers). If a value is unknown, the metric is omitted instead of being exported as 0 (see “Omitted series” below).

Process and configuration

Metric Type Labels Meaning
keen_pbr_build_info gauge version, commit, firewall_backend Always 1; build identity.
keen_pbr_process_start_time_seconds gauge - Unix start time; uptime is time() - keen_pbr_process_start_time_seconds.
keen_pbr_active_rules gauge - Number of applied firewall rules.
keen_pbr_config_reload_last_success_timestamp_seconds gauge - Unix time of the last completed config apply (startup counts). Omitted until the first one.
keen_pbr_config_reload_errors_total counter - Failed config reloads and applies (parse, validation, prepare or apply failures).
keen_pbr_list_last_update_timestamp_seconds gauge list Unix time of the last successful check of a remote (URL) list, whether or not its content changed. Omitted until the first successful refresh after startup.
keen_pbr_list_update_errors_total counter list Failed refresh attempts of a remote list.

Errors

keen_pbr_errors_total{subsystem} counts errors by subsystem. All values are always present, zeros included: firewall_apply (applying firewall rules), netlink (setting up routes), set_write (writing addresses to sets), conntrack, dns_parse (parsing DNS packets), dns_tcp_partial (incomplete DNS-over-TCP messages) and dns_late_write (failed deferred writes after a DNS answer).

Probes (urltest / icmptest)

A probe is a periodic check of a channel: a request to a URL (urltest) or a ping (icmptest). Labels: outbound (the channel being checked), test_outbound (the probe group), interface, type (urltest or icmptest).

Metric Type Meaning
keen_pbr_probe_attempts_total counter Accepted probe results.
keen_pbr_probe_successes_total counter Successful probe results.
keen_pbr_probe_packets_sent_total counter ICMP echo requests sent. type="icmptest" only.
keen_pbr_probe_packets_received_total counter ICMP echo replies received. type="icmptest" only.
keen_pbr_probe_up gauge 1 if the last probe succeeded, 0 if it failed.
keen_pbr_probe_last_success_timestamp_seconds gauge Unix time of the last successful probe.
keen_pbr_probe_latency_seconds gauge Latency of the last successful probe: ICMP is the mean of the received replies, URL is the request time. Sub-millisecond precision.
keen_pbr_probe_latency_min_seconds, keen_pbr_probe_latency_max_seconds gauge Fastest and slowest reply of the last successful ICMP probe. type="icmptest" only.
keen_pbr_urltest_selected gauge Labels group, outbound: 1 for the group’s currently selected outbound, 0 for the other members.
keen_pbr_urltest_selection_changes_total counter Label group: selection changes since the config was last applied (the counter resets on apply).

Omitted series

  • probe_up is omitted before the first probe of an outbound completed.
  • probe_latency_seconds, probe_latency_min_seconds and probe_latency_max_seconds are omitted when the last probe failed or no probe completed yet. In Grafana this shows up as a gap, never as a 0.
  • probe_last_success_timestamp_seconds is omitted until the first success.
  • list_last_update_timestamp_seconds and config_reload_last_success_timestamp_seconds are omitted until the first success.

Interception

Metrics for DNS interception and traffic (L7) analysis. path is dns or l7.

Metric Type Labels Meaning
keen_pbr_intercept_packets_total counter path = dns, l7 Packets inspected.
keen_pbr_intercept_matches_total counter path = dns, l7 Packets that matched a configured domain list.
keen_pbr_dns_hold_duration_seconds histogram - Time a DNS answer was held before its verdict.
keen_pbr_dns_queue_wait_duration_seconds histogram - Time a DNS packet waited in the receive queue.
keen_pbr_dns_hold_timeouts_total counter cause = batch_budget, admission_blocked, own_write_slow, late_batch_full, other Holds that reached their deadline.
keen_pbr_dns_late_writes_total counter - DNS writes completed after the packet was released.
keen_pbr_queue_overruns_total counter queue = nfqueue, nflog Kernel queue receive overruns.
keen_pbr_set_write_duration_seconds histogram path = dns, late_dns, l7 Dynamic set write time. Buckets (seconds): 0.0001, 0.00025, 0.0005, 0.001, 0.0025, 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, +Inf.
keen_pbr_set_writes_total counter kind = add, refresh Elements added (upserted) or timeout-refreshed.
keen_pbr_set_refresh_total counter result = skipped, deferred, dropped Cached-element refresh outcomes. dropped means the refresh queue was full.
keen_pbr_set_cache_lookups_total counter result = hit, miss Set cache lookups; a hit avoids a write before the verdict.
keen_pbr_set_cache_entries gauge - Remembered dynamic set elements.
keen_pbr_conntrack_requests_total counter - Conntrack cleanup requests.
keen_pbr_conntrack_deleted_total counter - Conntrack entries deleted.

Balancing and marked packets

These metrics exist only with the iptables firewall backend. A series with no data is omitted. Counters restart from zero when the firewall rules are rebuilt.

Metric Type Labels Meaning
keen_pbr_balance_classifications_total counter outbound, candidate, family = ipv4, ipv6 New connections that a balance group sent through the candidate channel.
keen_pbr_skip_marked_packets_total counter family = ipv4, ipv6 Packets keen-pbr skipped because they were already marked (General > Settings > General > Skip packets that are already marked).

The “slow write” share is derived from the le="0.025" bucket of keen_pbr_set_write_duration_seconds (writes slower than 25 ms).

Prometheus scrape configuration:

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: keen-pbr
    metrics_path: /metrics
    scrape_interval: 15s
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["router.example:12121"]
    basic_auth:
      username: admin
      password_file: /etc/prometheus/keen-pbr-password

Example queries:

# ICMP packet loss over 15 minutes, in percent (no data when nothing was sent)
100 * clamp(1 - increase(keen_pbr_probe_packets_received_total[15m])
    / (increase(keen_pbr_probe_packets_sent_total[15m]) > 0), 0, 1)

# Probe success rate over 15 minutes
100 * increase(keen_pbr_probe_successes_total[15m])
    / (increase(keen_pbr_probe_attempts_total[15m]) > 0)

# Average and 95th percentile latency per outbound over 1 hour (seconds)
avg_over_time(keen_pbr_probe_latency_seconds[1h])
quantile_over_time(0.95, keen_pbr_probe_latency_seconds[1h])

# DNS hold time p99 (seconds)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le)
    (rate(keen_pbr_dns_hold_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))

# Share of set writes slower than 25 ms, per path
1 - sum by (path) (rate(keen_pbr_set_write_duration_seconds_bucket{le="0.025"}[5m]))
  / (sum by (path) (rate(keen_pbr_set_write_duration_seconds_count[5m])) > 0)

# Errors in the last hour by subsystem
sum by (subsystem) (increase(keen_pbr_errors_total[1h])) > 0

Grafana dashboard and alerts

Import keen-pbr-dashboard.json into Grafana (Dashboards > New > Import). It needs a Prometheus data source with UID prometheus. The dashboard has job and outbound variables, a 30 s refresh, and the sections Status, Outbounds, DNS interception, Sets & lists and Errors. Use a scrape interval of 30 s or less: the bar panels compute increase() over one-minute windows.

Example alerting rules:

groups:
  - name: keen-pbr
    rules:
      - alert: KeenPbrDown
        expr: up{job="keen-pbr"} == 0
        for: 2m
      - alert: KeenPbrOutboundDown
        expr: keen_pbr_probe_up == 0
        for: 5m
        annotations:
          summary: "{{ $labels.outbound }} probe is failing ({{ $labels.test_outbound }})"
      - alert: KeenPbrProbeStale
        # Probes stopped completing (probe interval must be well below 30m).
        expr: increase(keen_pbr_probe_attempts_total[30m]) == 0
        for: 10m
      - alert: KeenPbrErrors
        expr: sum by (subsystem) (increase(keen_pbr_errors_total[10m])) > 0
        for: 5m
      - alert: KeenPbrDnsHoldSlow
        # 0.03 s is the default hold deadline (intercept hold_timeout_ms: 30).
        expr: >
          histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le)
            (rate(keen_pbr_dns_hold_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) > 0.03
        for: 10m
      - alert: KeenPbrQueueOverruns
        expr: sum by (queue) (increase(keen_pbr_queue_overruns_total[10m])) > 0
      - alert: KeenPbrListStale
        expr: time() - keen_pbr_list_last_update_timestamp_seconds > 86400
        for: 30m

POST /api/lists/refresh

Refreshes remote URL-backed lists from the active daemon config.

  • If name is provided, only that URL-backed list is refreshed.
  • If name is omitted, all URL-backed lists are refreshed.
  • If list contents changed and that affects routing or DNS, keen-pbr applies the changes immediately.
bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:12121/api/lists/refresh \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"apple"}'

Refresh all URL-backed lists:

bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:12121/api/lists/refresh

Request Body (optional) 

{
  "name": "apple"
}
  • name (optional string): List name to refresh.

Response (200) 

{
  "status": "ok",
  "message": "Lists refreshed and runtime reloaded",
  "refreshed_lists": ["apple", "google"],
  "changed_lists": ["apple"],
  "failed_lists": [],
  "reloaded": true
}

Success payload fields:

  • refreshed_lists (array[string]): URL-backed lists that were refreshed.
  • changed_lists (array[string]): Refreshed lists whose cached contents changed.
  • failed_lists (array[string]): URL-backed lists that could not be refreshed.
  • reloaded (boolean): Whether the changes were applied because the changed lists are in use.

Status / Error Behavior

  • 200: Refresh operation completed.
  • 400: Requested list exists but is not URL-backed.
  • 404: Requested list not found.
  • 409: Refresh rejected: there is an unsaved config draft or another operation is already running.

Error response body:

{
  "error": "human-readable message"
}

GET /api/config

Returns the current configuration and a flag showing whether an unsaved draft exists. The api settings (password, CORS) are not included. The response also contains list refresh state.

bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:12121/api/config

Response 

{
  "config": {
    "daemon": { "pid_file": "/var/run/keen-pbr.pid", "cache_dir": "/var/cache/keen-pbr" },
    "outbounds": [],
    "lists": {},
    "route": {}
  },
  "is_draft": false,
  "list_refresh_state": {}
}

is_draft is true when a config was submitted via POST /api/config but not yet saved to disk.

Error Response (500) 

{
  "error": "Cannot open config file"
}

POST /api/config

Validates the submitted JSON as a config file and keeps it in memory as a draft. Nothing is written to disk and routing does not change. To save and apply the draft, call POST /api/config/save.

The api field in the request is ignored.

bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:12121/api/config \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @new-config.json

Response 

{
  "status": "ok",
  "message": "Config staged in memory"
}

Error Response (400 — validation error) 

{
  "error": "Validation failed",
  "validation_errors": [
    { "path": "outbounds[0].interface", "message": "interface is required" }
  ]
}

POST /api/config/save

Starts saving the draft to disk and applying the configuration in the background. 202 means only that the operation was accepted, not that it has finished.

bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:12121/api/config/save

Accepted response (202) 

{
  "operation_id": "op-123",
  "status": "accepted"
}

Error Response (400 — no draft) 

{
  "error": "No staged config to save"
}

Other errors: 400 (the draft failed validation), 409 (another operation is already running), 500.

After 202, watch the lifecycle_operation field in GET /api/health/service, or subscribe to /api/status/events, until the operation finishes.

If applying failed after the file was saved, GET /api/health/service shows rollback_available: true. The file stays new. To return to the previous config, call POST /api/config/rollback (409 if there is nothing to roll back or another operation is running). POST /api/config/discard only drops an unsaved draft; it changes neither the file nor routing.

GET /api/runtime/outbounds

Returns the current state of outbounds: which channel a urltest group has selected right now (the group picks the channel with the lowest latency on its own), whether an interface is reachable, and whether it was switched off after a series of failures.

bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:12121/api/runtime/outbounds

Response 

{
  "outbounds": [
    {
      "tag": "vpn",
      "type": "interface",
      "status": "healthy",
      "interfaces": [
        { "outbound_tag": "vpn", "interface_name": "tun0", "status": "active" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "tag": "auto_select",
      "type": "urltest",
      "status": "healthy",
      "interfaces": [
        { "outbound_tag": "vpn", "interface_name": "tun0", "status": "active" },
        { "outbound_tag": "vpn2", "interface_name": "tun1", "status": "backup" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
  • type: interface, table, blackhole, ignore, urltest or icmptest.
  • Outbound status: healthy (working), degraded (partly working), unavailable (no usable path), unknown.
  • status in interfaces: active (traffic goes through it), backup (standby), degraded, unavailable (switched off after a series of failures), unknown. In a urltest group the selected channel is active.
  • Optional fields: latency_ms, probe_target, detail and packet counters.

POST /api/routing/test

Shows which outbound traffic to a domain or IP address will use. For a domain it first resolves the IP addresses. It then checks the routing rules against the lists (the expected outbound) and the firewall sets (the actual outbound). This helps find a mismatch without restarting the daemon.

bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:12121/api/routing/test \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"target": "example.com", "proto": "tcp", "dest_port": 443}'

The optional packet fields (proto: tcp, udp, or other; dest_port, src_addr, src_port, and dscp) let you test rules that filter by port, address, or DSCP . Without them, only list membership of the target is checked.

Response 

{
  "target": "example.com",
  "is_domain": true,
  "resolved_ips": ["93.184.216.34"],
  "results": [
    {
      "ip": "93.184.216.34",
      "expected_outbound": "vpn",
      "actual_outbound": "vpn",
      "ok": true,
      "list_match": { "list": "my_domains", "via": "domain" }
    }
  ],
  "warnings": [],
  "rule_diagnostics": [],
  "no_matching_rule": false
}
  • ok means the expected and actual outbound match. Instead of an outbound name you may see (default) (no rule matched, traffic uses the default) or (unknown) (could not be determined).
  • warnings holds non-fatal warnings, for example a DNS error. rule_diagnostics is a per-rule breakdown (shown in the web interface). no_matching_rule is true when no rule matched.

GET /api/health/routing

Returns a report on whether routes and the firewall are set up correctly: firewall rules with packet marks (an fwmark is a number the kernel uses to pick a route), route tables, and the rules that select a table. The report is refreshed in the background, so right after startup it may briefly show an incomplete result.

bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:12121/api/health/routing

Response 

{
  "overall": "ok",
  "firewall_backend": "iptables",
  "firewall": {
    "chain_present": true,
    "prerouting_hook_present": true,
    "verification_state": "verified",
    "detail": "ok"
  },
  "firewall_rules": [
    {
      "set_name": "<direct>",
      "action": "mark",
      "expected_fwmark": "0x00010000",
      "actual_fwmark": "0x00010000",
      "status": "ok"
    }
  ],
  "route_tables": [
    {
      "table_id": 150,
      "outbound_tag": "vpn",
      "expected_interface": "tun0",
      "expected_gateway": "10.8.0.1",
      "table_exists": true,
      "default_route_present": true,
      "interface_matches": true,
      "gateway_matches": true,
      "status": "ok"
    }
  ],
  "policy_rules": [
    {
      "fwmark": "0x00010000",
      "fwmask": "0x00ff0000",
      "expected_table": 150,
      "priority": 1000,
      "rule_present_v4": true,
      "rule_present_v6": true,
      "status": "ok"
    }
  ]
}

firewall.verification_state is verified, unavailable (firewall data not available) or failed. firewall.detail is ok on success and describes the cause otherwise. The optional warnings array lists warnings (for example, NAT is not set up or strict rp_filter is on); they do not affect overall.

Overall status values:

  • ok — all checks passed
  • degraded — one or more checks failed
  • error — an exception prevented checks from completing

Check status values:

  • ok — check passed
  • missing — expected element not found in kernel
  • mismatch — element found but configuration differs

Error Response (500) 

{
  "overall": "error",
  "error": "failed to connect to netlink socket"
}

GET /api/dns/test

Streams interception events as Server-Sent Events (the server sends events as they happen). HELLO comes first. The DNS check in the web interface uses this stream: it requests a special marker domain (check.keen-pbr.fyi) and waits for it to appear in the stream.

  • show=keen-pbr (default): only marker events. The stream closes when the matching marker arrives. Pass domain=<marker> to keep your check separate from others.
  • show=all (or show=full): the stream stays open and shows DNS queries, TLS SNI , HTTP Host, QUIC Initial and markers, including domains that are not in any list.

show=all exposes the traffic of every client, so it works only when API authentication is on. Without it the response is 403. The default view is always available. An invalid show or domain returns 400.

bash
curl -N -u admin:password 'http://127.0.0.1:12121/api/dns/test?show=all'

Stream Example 

data: {"type":"HELLO"}

data: {"type":"INTERCEPT","seq":42,"ts_ms":1712345678123,"source":"dns","client_ip":"192.168.1.10","domain":"example.com","lists":["streaming"],"ips":["203.0.113.7"],"added":1,"refreshed":0,"errors":0,"hold_us":180,"timed_out":false}

item.title: FAQ
item.description:
What firewall backend will be used?

It depends on daemon.firewall_backend. The default is "auto": keen-pbr uses nftables if the nft command is available, and iptables/ipset otherwise. On Keenetic, iptables/ipset is always used.

How do I reload lists without restarting the service?

Run the command for your platform:

bash
/opt/etc/init.d/S80keen-pbr reload
bash
service keen-pbr reload
bash
systemctl reload keen-pbr

This is a full reload: it re-downloads all remote lists and re-applies the firewall and routing rules.

In the keen-pbr-headless build this command does not work. To re-download the lists and apply them, run keen-pbr download --reload.

What reapply-firewall does
On Keenetic there is also /opt/etc/init.d/S80keen-pbr reapply-firewall. It re-verifies the routing tables and starts the urltest channel checks immediately, but does not re-download lists.

What happens if a remote list URL is unreachable at startup?

keen-pbr uses the cached copy from daemon.cache_dir if available. If there is no cache either, a list that has only url stays empty until a download succeeds; keen-pbr keeps retrying in the background.

How does the urltest outbound select the best link?

Every interval_ms, keen-pbr sends an HTTP request to the configured url through each link and measures the round-trip latency. With strategy: "priority", the link with the lowest latency is selected. If the new best link is faster than the current one by less than tolerance_ms, keen-pbr does not switch. Links are checked group by group: the next group in outbound_groups is used only when no link in the previous one works.

If a link fails failure_threshold checks in a row, keen-pbr stops using it for timeout_ms, then tries it again with a few checks. This keeps traffic from bouncing between links while one of them is unstable.

Can I route DNS queries through a VPN?

Yes. Use the detour field in dns.servers to bind DNS queries for that server to a specific outbound:

{
  "servers": [
    {
      "tag": "vpn_dns",
      "address": "10.8.0.1",
      "detour": "vpn"
    }
  ]
}

What’s the list file format?

One entry per line. Supported formats:

  • IPv4 address: 93.184.216.34
  • IPv6 address: 2606:2800:220:1:248:1893:25c8:1946
  • CIDR : 10.0.0.0/8
  • Domain: example.com (automatically includes all sub-domains)
    • entries like *.example.com work the same way as example.com
  • Lines starting with # are comments and are skipped
  • Empty lines are skipped

How do I verify routing is correctly applied?

Run:

bash
keen-pbr status

keen-pbr compares the firewall rules, routing tables and ip rule entries in the kernel with what it expects and marks each item OK, MISSING, MISMATCH or ERROR. The same check is in the web UI: the Diagnostics panel on the General > Dashboard page. To check a specific site, click Where does this traffic go? on the same page or run keen-pbr test-routing <domain-or-ip>.

Why does a check from the router itself not go through the VPN?

The Process router’s own traffic (shown in Advanced settings mode) option (General > Settings > General) is off by default: the rules apply to traffic from devices on your local network, not to commands like curl in the router’s SSH console. Test routing from a device on the network. Also, if the Processed (inbound) interfaces list is not empty, make sure the device connects through one of those interfaces.

Can I combine multiple sources in one list?

Yes. url, domains, ip_cidrs, and file can all be set in the same list entry and the data is combined:

{
  "lists": {
    "combined": {
      "url": "https://example.com/remote.txt",
      "domains": ["extra.example.com"],
      "ip_cidrs": ["192.168.100.0/24"],
      "file": "./local.txt"
    }
  }
}
The web UI can combine only ip_cidrs and domains. Do not combine them with url or file: the web UI does not support this, and a future version may reject it.

item.title: Full Reference Config
item.description:
This page shows one full configuration example with comments, including platform-specific settings marked in the example. Remove settings that are unsupported on your target platform before applying it.

You can write // comments in config.json. Replace sample interfaces, addresses, and file paths with values from your network before applying it.

List names, outbound tags, and DNS server tags must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ and must be at most 24 characters.
config.json
{
  // keen-pbr version this config was written for (X.Y.Z).
  // Set automatically when you save from the Web UI; keep it when editing by hand.
  "version": "3.4.0",

  // Optional device label shown in the browser title and beneath the keen-pbr logo.
  // Maximum length: 128 characters. Default: empty (the standard keen-pbr
  // branding is used).
  "device_name": "Home router",

  // General keen-pbr service settings.
  // All fields in this section are optional.
  "daemon": {
    // Path to the PID file (the file holding the service's process number).
    // Default: no file is written when omitted.
    "pid_file": "/var/run/keen-pbr.pid",

    // Directory used for remote-list cache files and cache metadata.
    // Default: "/var/cache/keen-pbr".
    "cache_dir": "/var/cache/keen-pbr",

    // Which firewall to use.
    // Supported values: "auto", "iptables", "nftables".
    // Default: "auto".
    "firewall_backend": "auto",

    // Do not process packets that another program has already marked (fwmark).
    // Default: true (also when set to null).
    "skip_marked_packets": true,

    // Clear the dynamic sets (domain IPs from DNS replies and connections) on
    // every config apply or service restart. Default: false (also when set to null).
    "clear_dynamic_sets_on_apply": false,

    // Optional initial hash table size for ipsets created by the iptables backend.
    // Has no effect with nftables. Minimum: 1; maximum: 2147483648. Omit or set
    // to null to use the ipset default (1024).
    // Changing it recreates the sets and empties the dynamic sets.
    "ipset_hashsize": null,

    // Optional maximum element count for ipsets created by the iptables backend.
    // Has no effect with nftables. Minimum: 1; maximum: 4294967295. Omit or set
    // to null to use the ipset default (65536).
    // Changing it recreates the sets and empties the dynamic sets.
    "ipset_maxelem": null,

    // Do not refill list sets on SIGUSR1, urltest/icmptest switches and
    // interface changes; only rules are updated. Default: true.
    "reuse_static_sets_on_runtime_refresh": true,

    // Route IPv6 traffic. Default: true (also when set to null).
    // If the system has no IPv6 support, keen-pbr logs an error and continues
    // in IPv4-only mode.
    "ipv6_enabled": true,

    // Block traffic when an interface outbound is down instead of letting it
    // go out through the normal connection. Default: false.
    "strict_enforcement": false,

    // What to do with traffic when strict_enforcement applies.
    // Supported values: "unreachable" (return a network error) or "blackhole"
    // (silently drop packets). Default: "unreachable".
    "strict_enforcement_action": "unreachable",

    // Maximum allowed size for downloaded remote content such as URL-backed lists.
    // Default: 8388608 bytes (8 MiB).
    "max_file_size_bytes": 8388608,

    // How many bytes of iptables/nft output to read when checking firewall rules
    // (`keen-pbr status`, status page). 0 means no limit.
    // Default: 262144.
    "firewall_verify_max_bytes": 262144,

    // How many seconds to wait for keen-pbr's helper scripts (for example the
    // dnsmasq script) before stopping them. Minimum: 1. Default: 30.
    "exec_timeout_seconds": 30,

    // How many seconds to give a script to exit after it is stopped before it
    // is killed. Minimum: 0. Default: 2.
    "exec_kill_grace_seconds": 2
  },

  // Embedded HTTP API and web UI settings.
  // WARNING: This section is NOT available in keen-pbr-headless package
  "api": {
    // Enable or disable the HTTP API and the web UI.
    // Default: false.
    "enabled": true,

    // Address and port the API server listens on.
    // Default: "0.0.0.0:12121".
    "listen": "0.0.0.0:12121",

    // Maximum request body size in bytes. Minimum: 1024. Default: 1048576.
    "max_request_body_bytes": 1048576,

    // How many seconds to wait for an HTTP request from the client.
    // Minimum: 1. Default: 15.
    "read_timeout_seconds": 15,

    // How many seconds to send an HTTP response to the client.
    // Minimum: 1. Default: 15.
    "write_timeout_seconds": 15,

    // How many seconds to keep a connection open between requests.
    // Minimum: 1. Default: 20.
    "keep_alive_timeout_seconds": 20,

    // Password login for the API and the web UI. Default: disabled.
    // With enabled: true, password_hash is required: create it with
    // `keen-pbr hash-password --update` or in the web UI (Security).
    "authentication": {
      "enabled": false
    },

    // Site addresses (origins) allowed to call the API from a browser.
    // Exact http:// or https:// addresses only, no path or wildcards.
    // Omit this object when no CORS origins are needed.
    "cors": {
      "allowed_origins": ["https://router.example"]
    }
  },

  // All supported outbound types.
  // An outbound is the channel traffic goes through: an interface, a routing
  // table, a block, and so on. Tags are referenced by route rules, DNS server
  // detours, and list detours.
  // "type" is required and supports: interface, table, blackhole, ignore,
  // urltest, and icmptest.
  "outbounds": [
    {
      // "interface" sends traffic through a specific network interface.
      "type": "interface",

      // Unique outbound tag.
      // Default: no default, required.
      "tag": "vpn",

      // Egress interface name.
      // Default: no default, required for type="interface".
      "interface": "wg0",

      // Optional IPv4 gateway for the interface outbound. Set to "auto" to
      // discover the unique lowest-metric matching default route in the main
      // table; omit it for a gatewayless route.
      // Default: null
      "gateway": "10.8.0.1",

      // Optional IPv6 gateway for the interface outbound. Set to "auto" to
      // discover the unique lowest-metric matching default route in the main
      // table; omit it for a gatewayless route.
      // Default: null
      "gateway6": "2001:db8::1",

      // This outbound's own strict_enforcement value.
      // Takes precedence over daemon.strict_enforcement when set.
      // Default: inherit daemon.strict_enforcement.
      "strict_enforcement": true,

      // This outbound's own value of daemon.strict_enforcement_action.
      // Supported values: "unreachable" or "blackhole".
      // Default: inherit daemon.strict_enforcement_action.
      "strict_enforcement_action": "unreachable"
    },
    
    {
      // Another interface outbound, for example for the normal internet (WAN) connection.
      "type": "interface",
      "tag": "wan",
      "interface": "eth0",
      // Set the gateway explicitly, or use "auto" to detect it from the matching
      // default route in the main table.
      "gateway": "auto"
    },
    
    {
      // "table" reuses an existing kernel routing table.
      "type": "table",

      // Unique outbound tag.
      "tag": "wan_as_table",

      // ID of an existing Linux routing table.
      // Default: no default, required for type="table".
      "table": 254
    },

    {
      // "blackhole" drops matching traffic.
      "type": "blackhole",

      // Unique outbound tag.
      "tag": "block"
    },

    {
      // "ignore" keeps matching traffic on the system's normal routing;
      // keen-pbr does not touch it.
      "type": "ignore",

      // Unique outbound tag.
      "tag": "direct"
    },

    {
      // "urltest" probes several candidate outbounds and selects one automatically.
      "type": "urltest",

      // Unique outbound tag.
      "tag": "auto_select",

      // Probe URL used for latency / reachability checks.
      // Default: no default, required for type="urltest".
      "url": "https://www.gstatic.com/generate_204",

      // Probe interval in milliseconds.
      // Default: 180000 for urltest; 60000 for icmptest.
      "interval_ms": 180000,

      // Timeout for each individual probe attempt in milliseconds.
      // Default: 5000 for urltest; 1000 for icmptest.
      // Omit this field or set it to null to use the default for the outbound type.
      "probe_timeout_ms": 5000,

      // Do not switch if the new candidate is only slightly better than the current one.
      // Minimum: 0 ms. Default: 100 for urltest.
      "tolerance_ms": 100,

      // Selection strategy: "priority" (default) uses one selected link.
      // "balance" (not on Keenetic) spreads new connections over the working
      // links of the first working group in proportion to their weight.
      "strategy": "priority",

      // Kept for compatibility with older configs; it has no effect:
      // urltest always blocks traffic when no link works.
      "strict_enforcement": true,

      // What to do with open conntrack connections when another link is selected.
      // Supported values: "preserve" (default) or "delete". If the selected
      // link stops working, the entries are always deleted.
      "conntrack_on_switch": "preserve",

      // Ordered outbound groups.
      // Default: no default, required for type="urltest".
      // Groups are tried in array order (first group first).
      "outbound_groups": [
        {
          // Members of this group. Supported types: interface, table.
          "members": [
            // "weight" (1-100, default 1) is the share of new connections
            // under strategy "balance"; ignored by "priority".
            { "outbound": "vpn", "weight": 7 },
            { "outbound": "wan_as_table", "weight": 3 }
          ]
        },
        {
          // If the first group does not work, keen-pbr switches to this one.
          // If no link works at all, traffic is blocked.
          "members": [{ "outbound": "wan" }]
        }
      ],

      // Probe retry behavior.
      "retry": {
        // How many times to try the probe, including the first attempt.
        // Default: 1.
        "attempts": 3,

        // Delay between retries in milliseconds.
        // Default: 1000.
        "interval_ms": 1000
      },

      // Circuit breaker settings.
      "circuit_breaker": {
        // The circuit breaker temporarily disables an unstable outbound.
        // How many failures in a row open it (the outbound is disabled).
        // Minimum: 1; maximum: 20. Default: 5.
        "failure_threshold": 5,

        // How many successful probes are needed to return to normal.
        // Minimum: 1; maximum: 20. Default: 2.
        "success_threshold": 2,

        // How many milliseconds after opening the outbound gets a trial probe
        // (half-open). Minimum: 1; maximum: 86400000.
        // Default: 30000 for urltest; for icmptest, the larger of 60000 and interval_ms.
        "timeout_ms": 30000,

        // How many trial probes are allowed while half-open.
        // Minimum: 1; maximum: 10. Default: 1.
        "half_open_max_requests": 1
      }
    },

    {
      // "icmptest" sends ICMP Echo probes through candidate outbounds and
      // selects a healthy candidate automatically.
      "type": "icmptest",
      "tag": "auto_ping",

      // Probe interval in milliseconds. Default: 60000.
      "interval_ms": 60000,

      // ICMP Echo requests per candidate run. Minimum: 1; maximum: 10.
      // Default: 3.
      "count": 3,

      // Maximum failed packets allowed in a successful run. Minimum: 0.
      // It must be less than count. Default: 0.
      "max_failed": 0,

      // Pause between sequential ICMP attempts. Minimum: 100 ms; maximum:
      // 1000 ms. Default: 200.
      "packet_interval_ms": 200,

      // Timeout for each ICMP attempt. Runtime range: 100-5000 ms.
      // Default: 1000.
      "probe_timeout_ms": 1000,

      // Replies slower than this are failures. Minimum: 1 ms and it must not
      // exceed probe_timeout_ms. Default: 500.
      "max_rtt_ms": 500,

      // Do not switch when the new candidate is only slightly better.
      // Minimum: 0 ms. Default: 10.
      "tolerance_ms": 10,

      // Keep or delete open conntrack connections when another link
      // is selected. Supported values: "preserve" (default) or "delete".
      "conntrack_on_switch": "preserve",

      // Ordered groups (first tried first) of explicit outbound/target
      // members. Required for type="icmptest". Every member requires
      // "outbound" and "target"; "weight" (1-100, default 1) is optional.
      "outbound_groups": [
        {
          "members": [
            {
              // Interface or table outbound tag.
              "outbound": "vpn",
              // IPv4 or IPv6 address to ping through that outbound.
              "target": "1.1.1.1"
            },
            {
              "outbound": "wan",
              "target": "9.9.9.9",
              "weight": 3
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],

  // Lists may use one or more of these sources: url, domains, ip_cidrs, file.
  "lists": {

    "inline_domains": {
      // Inline domains.
      // Domains match the domain itself and its subdomains.
      // Wildcards such as "*.example.com" are optional: "example.com" has the
      // same effect.
      "domains": ["example.com", "othersite.net"],

      // Minimum lifetime of IPs learned through DNS and L7 interception.
      // Omitted, 0, and values below 1000 ms use intercept.min_ttl_ms.
      // Values of 1000 ms or more are truncated to whole seconds. A DNS
      // record TTL may raise the timeout up to intercept.max_ttl_ms. This is
      // separate from the refresh interval for remote lists.
      "ttl_ms": 86400000
    },

    "inline_ips": {
      // Inline IPv4/IPv6 addresses or CIDRs.
      "ip_cidrs": [
        "93.184.216.34",
        "10.0.0.0/8",
        "2001:db8::1",
        "2001:db8::/32"
      ]
    },

    "remote_list": {
      // Remote list URL.
      "url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/v2fly/domain-list-community/refs/heads/master/data/apple",

      // Optional outbound used to download this list.
      // Interface, table and urltest outbounds are supported.
      // Default: null (use the system's normal routing)
      "detour": "auto_select",

      // Minimum lifetime of IPs learned through DNS and L7 interception.
      // Omitted, 0, and values below 1000 ms use intercept.min_ttl_ms.
      // Values of 1000 ms or more are truncated to whole seconds. A DNS
      // record TTL may raise the timeout up to intercept.max_ttl_ms. This is
      // separate from the refresh interval for remote lists.
      "ttl_ms": 86400000
    },
  
    "local_file_list": {
      // Local list file path.
      "file": "/etc/keen-pbr/local.lst",
      
      // Minimum lifetime of IPs learned through DNS and L7 interception.
      // Omitted, 0, and values below 1000 ms use intercept.min_ttl_ms.
      // Values of 1000 ms or more are truncated to whole seconds. A DNS
      // record TTL may raise the timeout up to intercept.max_ttl_ms. This is
      // separate from the refresh interval for remote lists.
      "ttl_ms": 86400000
    },

    "mixed_sources": {
      // You can combine several sources in one list,
      // but separate lists are usually easier to maintain.
      "domains": ["intranet.example"],
      "ip_cidrs": ["192.168.50.0/24"],
      "file": "/etc/keen-pbr/mixed.lst",
      "url": "https://example.com/mixed.lst",
      "detour": "vpn",
      // ttl_ms applies to domain sources in this list. See the inline_domains
      // example above for sizing guidance.
      "ttl_ms": 86400000
    }
  },

  // DNS configuration. Interception fills dynamic sets without a resolver.
  "dns": {
    // Optional: per-list DNS servers via dnsmasq.
    // Default: "none" (keen-pbr does not touch the system resolver).
    // Set to "dnsmasq" to resolve domains from specific lists through chosen
    // DNS servers. With "none", dns.rules and fallback are not used and a
    // warning is logged.
    "resolver_integration": "none",

    // Which dnsmasq instance to use: "uci:<section>" (OpenWrt),
    // "entware:default" (Keenetic) or "systemd:<unit>.service" (Debian).
    // Default: empty, the instance is chosen automatically. Fill it in only if
    // `keen-pbr dnsmasq detect` finds several instances.
    "dnsmasq_instance": "uci:cfg01411c",

    // All supported DNS server styles.
    "servers": [
      {
        // Plain DNS server with a fixed address, no detour.
        "tag": "google_dns",

        // Supported values: "static" (default) or "keenetic".
        // Default: "static".
        "type": "static",

        // DNS server address (for type="static").
        // Default: no default, required for type="static".
        "address": "8.8.8.8"
      },

      {
        // DNS server reached through an interface outbound.
        "tag": "vpn_dns",
        "address": "10.8.0.1:5353",

        // Optional outbound used to contact this DNS server.
        // Supported: interface, table, urltest outbounds.
        // Not allowed: blackhole, ignore.
        // Default: use the system's normal routing.
        "detour": "vpn"
      },

      {
        // DNS server reached through a urltest outbound.
        "tag": "auto_dns",
        "address": "[2606:4700:4700::1111]:53",
        "detour": "auto_select"
      },

      {
        // [Only on Keenetic and Netcraze platforms]
        // Reuse the router's built-in DNS settings through RCI.
        // Configure DoT/DoH on the router first, then add this Keenetic DNS server.
        "tag": "keenetic_dns",
        "type": "keenetic"
      }

    ],

    // "List domains -> DNS server" rules (only work when resolver_integration: "dnsmasq").
    "rules": [
      {
        // Whether this DNS rule is active. Default: true when omitted or null.
        "enabled": true,

        // Lists whose domains should be resolved by this server.
        "list": ["inline_domains"],

        // DNS server tag to use.
        "server": "vpn_dns",

        // Allow answers that resolve to private/local IP ranges.
        // Default: false.
        "allow_domain_rebinding": false
      }
    ],

    // DNS servers for domains that match no rule
    // (only work when resolver_integration: "dnsmasq").
    // Default: empty (servers from resolv.conf are used).
    "fallback": ["google_dns"]
  },

  // Traffic interception. All fields below have defaults. If the kernel lacks
  // something, only that part (DNS or L7) is turned off; see the status page.
  "intercept": {
    // Routing by domain. When false, domain rules do not work;
    // IP and CIDR rules still do.
    "enabled": true,

    // Minimum and maximum lifetime of an address in a set, in milliseconds.
    // At least 1000, min_ttl_ms must not exceed max_ttl_ms; values are rounded to seconds.
    "min_ttl_ms": 300000,
    "max_ttl_ms": 86400000,
    "dns": {
      // Read plain (unencrypted) DNS replies on port 53.
      "enabled": true,

      // NFQUEUE queue number (1-65535, except 64511 and 65023: Keenetic uses them).
      "queue_num": 9053,

      // How many milliseconds to hold a DNS reply while the address is added to the set (5-500).
      "hold_timeout_ms": 30,
      "marker": {
        // Domain and IPv4 answer used to check that DNS interception works.
        "domain": "check.keen-pbr.fyi",
        "answer_ipv4": "127.0.0.88"
      }
    },
    "l7": {
      // Learn addresses from the connections themselves: the TLS name (SNI), the HTTP Host header, QUIC.
      "enabled": true,

      // NFLOG group number (1-65535, except 64511 and 65023).
      "nflog_group": 9054,

      // Which protocols to parse.
      "tls": true,
      "http": true,
      "quic": true
    }
  },

  // Range of fwmark values.
  // This section is optional.
  "fwmark": {
    // First fwmark (packet label) assigned to outbounds, as a hex string.
    // Default: "0x00010000".
    "start": "0x00010000",

    // Fwmark bitmask as a hex string.
    // Must contain one or more consecutive F nibbles.
    // Default: "0x00FF0000".
    "mask": "0x00FF0000"
  },

  // Routing table numbers and `ip rule` priorities.
  // This section is optional.
  "iproute": {
    // First routing table ID used for auto-allocated outbound tables.
    // Default: 150.
    // Do not use reserved IDs: 0, 128, 250-260 and everything from 32000.
    "table_start": 150,

    // First priority of the `ip rule` entries.
    // Default: null, which inherits table_start.
    "rule_priority_start": null,

    // Apply route rules to, and learn domains from, the router's own traffic.
    // Default: false (only traffic of devices in the network; DNS server detour works either way).
    "process_router_traffic": false
  },

  // Routing rules.
  "route": {
    // Optional ingress interface filter.
    // If omitted or empty, keen-pbr processes packets from any interface.
    // Default: no filter.
    "inbound_interfaces": ["br0", "wg-lan"],

    "rules": [
      {
        // Simple rule: traffic to domains and IPs from the lists goes to the outbound.
        // enabled defaults to true when omitted or set to null.
        "list": ["inline_domains", "remote_list"],
        "outbound": "auto_select"
      },

      {
        // Send addresses from a list through an existing routing table.
        "list": ["inline_ips"],
        "outbound": "wan_as_table"
      },

      {
        // Example rule with every condition: DSCP, protocol, addresses and ports.
        "enabled": true,

        // Only if the destination domain or IP is in the list
        "list": ["mixed_sources"],

        // Only if the protocol is TCP
        // Possible values: null (for any protocol), tcp, udp, tcp/udp
        "proto": "tcp",

        // Only if the DSCP tag (traffic priority) equals this value.
        // Integer from 1 to 63.
        "dscp": 46,

        // Only if the source IP matches.
        // One IP or CIDR; several separated by commas. A leading `!` inverts the condition.
        "src_addr": "192.168.10.0/24,192.168.20.0/24",

        // Only if the destination IP matches. Same format as src_addr.
        "dest_addr": "203.0.113.0/24",

        // [Only for nftables when combining src_port with a dest_port list]
        // On iptables, remove src_port when dest_port contains a port list.
        // Only if the source port matches.
        // One port, several separated by commas, or a range
        "src_port": "1024-65535",

        // Only if the destination port matches.
        // One port, several separated by commas, or a range; a leading `!` inverts the condition
        "dest_port": "443,8443",

        // Send matched traffic to this outbound
        "outbound": "vpn"
      },

      {
        // "list" can be omitted if another condition is present.
        // This example blocks DNS requests to any address except the trusted subnet.
        "proto": "udp",
        "dest_port": "53",
        "dest_addr": "!10.10.0.0/16",
        "outbound": "block"
      },

      {
        // Example exception: an "ignore" outbound placed before broader VPN rules.
        "src_addr": "192.168.1.0/24",
        "dest_addr": "192.168.0.0/16",
        "outbound": "direct"
      },

      {
        // IPv6 example: route HTTPS traffic to a documentation subnet via VPN.
        "proto": "tcp",
        "src_addr": "2001:db8:10::/64",
        "dest_addr": "2001:db8:203::/48",
        "dest_port": "443",
        "outbound": "vpn"
      },

      {
        // Example disabled rule kept for later use.
        "enabled": false,
        "list": ["inline_domains"],
        "proto": "tcp/udp",
        "dest_port": "!80,443",
        "outbound": "wan"
      },

      {
        // [Only for nftables]
        // "Everything else" rule for outgoing IPv4 traffic. Keep default_gateway rules
        // last. Traffic of devices in the network is covered by default; to include
        // the router's own traffic, set iproute.process_router_traffic to true.
        "default_gateway": "ipv4",
        "outbound": "auto_select"
      },

      {
        // [Only for nftables]
        // "Everything else" rule for outgoing IPv6 traffic. Keep it last.
        "default_gateway": "ipv6",
        "outbound": "auto_select"
      }
    ]
  },

  // Automatic refresh for URL-backed lists.
  // This section is optional.
  "lists_autoupdate": {
    // Enable or disable periodic refresh.
    // Default: false.
    "enabled": true,

    // Schedule: a 5-field cron expression.
    // Required when enabled=true.
    // No default value.
    "cron": "0 4 * * 0"
  }
}

Notes

  • dns.servers[].detour supports interface, table, and urltest outbounds, but not blackhole or ignore.
  • lists[].detour is useful when a remote list should be downloaded through a VPN or other non-default path.
  • route.rules[] must include at least one matching condition: list, dscp, src_port, dest_port, src_addr, dest_addr, or default_gateway.
  • dns.rules[].allow_domain_rebinding is mainly for internal domains that intentionally resolve to private IP ranges.

item.title: Multi-WAN Load Balancing
item.description:
This page is for a Debian or Ubuntu host connected to two internet providers, where new connections should be spread between them (multi-WAN). It describes the iptables firewall backend.

Load balancing is not available on Keenetic: the Keenetic build does not support it and rejects a configuration with "strategy": "balance". Use the router’s own multipath there. The nftables backend (OpenWrt 24+ with fw4, or any host with nft) supports balancing as well, see Outbounds. The step-by-step guide below targets iptables on Debian/Ubuntu, and the NAT , rp_filter and fwmark (a numeric mark on a packet) notes apply to every backend.

How it works

A urltest or icmptest outbound with "strategy": "balance" picks one of its working links for every new connection, in proportion to the link’s weight (1-100, default 1). The whole connection uses one link. Links that fail their checks are removed from the split and come back when they work again.

You set up two things on the system yourself: NAT on every provider and rp_filter (see below).

Choose the iptables backend
